title: ZPA Terraform resources: fields not sent, not read back, or written in several non-atomic steps
aliases: terraform zpa state does not match api
service edge assistant schedule destroy does nothing
user code verification failed after create
server group name blank on update
zia cloud config read error ignored

schedule-create-discards-server-id.statement: Creating the Service Edge assistant schedule discards the object the SDK returns from the POST, then stores the ID of the request as the resource ID. The request ID was read from the resource's own computed `id`, which is empty on a first create, so the first-create path sets an empty ID. Only the already-exists branch sets the real ID, by reading the singleton. An empty ID after create probably makes Terraform report an inconsistent result rather than record the resource (Terraform core behavior, inferred, not shown here).

redirection-create-skips-policy-set-look.statement: Creating a redirection rule never resolves `policy_set_id`. The schema makes it optional and computed, the create path expands it straight from the resource data, and the SDK builds the POST URL from it. The forwarding rule resource, by contrast, looks the policy set up by type when the argument is unset.

private-cloud-no-exporter-group-field.statement: The SDK's private cloud model has a `PrivateExporterGroupIDs` field and the provider's documentation names Private Exporter among the groups the resource associates, but the resource defines no argument for it and its Read and expand never touch it. A Private Exporter association cannot be configured, is not read into state, and is not part of what Terraform sends.

private-cloud-create-then-fire-drill-put.statement: Creating a private cloud with fire drill enabled is two writes. The provider clears `FireDrillEnabled` and the fire drill site from the POST, then sends them in a separate PUT after storing the new ID. If that PUT fails, the provider returns an error that says the cloud was created and to run apply again; it does not delete the cloud. The provider's comments say the API rejects fire drill on create; that is the provider's statement, not shown here.

These are separate fields of the SDK response. A response with only portal capabilities is not written to state, and one with only generic capabilities clears the portal capabilities attribute (the flattener returns nil).

capabilities-read-never-clears.statement: The capabilities rule Read sets `privileged_capabilities` only when the response lists at least one capability, and has no other branch. When the response has none, the previous value stays in state.

pra-console-read-never-clears-applicatio.statement: The PRA console Read sets `pra_application` only when the flattener returns a value, and the flattener returns nil when the response application has no ID. A removed application association leaves the previous block in state.

pra-approval-end-not-checked-against-sta.statement: The PRA approval time validator, called from create and update, checks that the start is not more than an hour in the past and that the end is at most a year after the start. It does not compare the end with the start, so an end before or equal to the start passes it.

api-server-group-put-name.title: How ZPA treats a server group PUT that has no name
api-server-group-put-name.blocks: saying whether an ordinary server group update blanks, keeps or rejects the name
api-server-group-put-name.detail: The client sends no name member when only other attributes changed. Whether ZPA keeps the stored name, clears it or returns an error is not shown by any captured source. Test in a scratch tenant: change only the description of a server group through Terraform and re-read the name.
